title: polypodium cambricum subsp. macaronesicum
intro: Polypodium cambricum subsp. macaronesicum, commonly known as the Madeira polypody, is a type of fern native to the Macaronesian region of the Atlantic Ocean. This plant has been traditionally used in herbal medicine to treat various ailments, offering health benefits such as reducing inflammation and improving respiratory conditions. The therapeutic actions of Polypodium cambricum subsp. macaronesicum are attributed to its ability to modulate the immune system, exhibit antioxidant properties, and act as a demulcent. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and other compounds that contribute to its medicinal properties.
